When--</hi>Supply from <reference osisRef="Isa.64.2">Is 64:2</reference>, "As when."<div eID="gen16608" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16609" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">terrible things--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.65.5">Psa 65:5</reference>).<div eID="gen16609" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16610" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">we looked not for--</hi>far exceeding the expectation of any of our nation; unparalleled before (<reference osisRef="Exod.34.10">Ex 34:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.68.8">Psa 68:8</reference>).<div eID="gen16610" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16611" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">camest down--</hi>on Mount Sinai.<div eID="gen16611" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16612" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">mountains flowed--</hi>Repeated from <reference osisRef="Isa.64.1">Is 64:1</reference>; they pray God to do the very same things for Israel now as in former ages. Gesenius, instead of "flowed" here, and "flow" in Is 64:1 , translates from a different Hebrew root, "quake ... quaked"; but "fire" melts and causes to flow, rather than to quake ( Is 64:2 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9515"/><div sID="gen16613" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9515"/><hi type="bold">4. perceived by the ear--</hi>Paul (<reference osisRef="1Cor.2.9">1Co 2:9</reference>) has for this, "nor have entered into the heart of man"; the virtual sense, sanctioned by his inspired authority; men might hear with the outward ear, but they could only by the Spirit "perceive" with the "heart" the spiritual significancy of God's acts, both those in relation to Israel, primarily referred to here, and those relating to the Gospel secondarily, which Paul refers to.<div eID="gen16613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16614" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">O God ... what he ... prepared--</hi>rather, "nor hath eye seen a god beside thee who doeth such things." They refer to God's past marvellous acts in behalf of Israel as a plea for His now interposing for His people; but the Spirit, as Paul by inspiration shows, contemplated further God's revelation in the Gospel, which abounds in marvellous paradoxes never before heard of by carnal ear, not to be understood by mere human sagacity, and when foretold by the prophets not fully perceived or credited; and even after the manifestation of Christ not to be understood save through the inward teaching of the Holy Ghost. These are partly past and present, and partly future; therefore Paul substitutes "prepared" for "doeth," though his context shows he includes all three. For "waiteth" he has "love Him"; godly waiting on Him must flow from love, and not mere fear. <div eID="gen16614" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9516"/><div sID="gen16615" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9516"/><hi type="bold">5. meetest--</hi>that is, Thou makest peace, or enterest into covenant with him (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.47.3">Is 47:3</reference>).<div eID="gen16615" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16616" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rejoiceth and worketh--</hi>that is, who with joyful willingness worketh [Gesenius] (<reference osisRef="Acts.10.35">Ac 10:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.7.17">Joh 7:17</reference>).<div eID="gen16616" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16617" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">those--</hi>Thou meetest "those," in apposition to "him" who represents a class whose characteristics "those that," &c., more fully describes.<div eID="gen16617" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16618" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">remember thee in thy ways--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.26.8">Is 26:8</reference>).<div eID="gen16618" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16619" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sinned--</hi>literally, "tripped," carrying on the figure in "ways."<div eID="gen16619" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16620" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in those is continuance--</hi>a plea to deprecate the continuance of God's wrath; it is not in Thy wrath that there is continuance (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.7">Is 54:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.54.8">8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.30.5">Psa 30:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.103.9">103:9</reference>), but in Thy ways ("those"), namely, of covenant mercy to Thy people (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.18-Mic.7.20">Mi 7:18-20</reference>; Mal 3:6); on the strength of the everlasting continuance of His covenant they infer by faith, "we shall be saved." God "remembered" for them His covenant (<reference osisRef="Ps.106.45">Psa 106:45</reference>), though they often "remembered not" Him (<reference osisRef="Ps.78.42">Psa 78:42</reference>). Castellio translates, "we have sinned for long in them ('thy ways'), and could we then be saved?" But they hardly would use such a plea when their very object was to be saved. <div eID="gen16620" type="x-p"/>

God "remembered" for them His covenant ( Psa 106:45 ), though they often "remembered not" Him ( Psa 78:42 ). Castellio translates, "we have sinned for long in them ('thy ways'), and could we then be saved?" But they hardly would use such a plea when their very object was to be saved.

True of Israel, everywhere now cut off by unbelief and by God's judgments from the congregation of the saints.<div eID="gen16621" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16622" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteousness--</hi>plural, "uncleanness" extended to every particular act of theirs, even to their prayers and praises. True of the best doings of the unregenerate (<reference osisRef="Phil.3.6-Phil.3.8">Php 3:6-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Titus.1.15">Tit 1:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.11.6">He 11:6</reference>).<div eID="gen16622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16623" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">filthy rags--</hi>literally, a "menstruous rag" (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.33">Le 15:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">20:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.1.17">La 1:17</reference>).<div eID="gen16623" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16624" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fade ... leaf--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.90.5">Psa 90:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.90.6">6</reference>). <div eID="gen16624" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 6. unclean thing-- legally unclean, as a leper. True of Israel, everywhere now cut off by unbelief and by God's judgments from the congregation of the saints. righteousness-- plural, "uncleanness" extended to every particular act of theirs, even to their prayers and praises. True of the best doings of the unregenerate ( Php 3:6-8 ; Tit 1:15 ; He 11:6 ). filthy rags-- literally, a "menstruous rag" ( Le 15:33 ; 20:18 ; La 1:17 ). fade ... leaf-- ( Psa 90:5 , 6 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9521"/><div sID="gen16631" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9521"/><hi type="bold">10. holy cities--</hi>No city but Jerusalem is called "the holy city" (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.2">Is 48:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">52:1</reference>); the plural, therefore, refers to the upper and the lower parts of the same city Jerusalem [Vitringa]; or all Judea was holy to God, so its cities were deemed "holy" [Maurer]. But the parallelism favors Vitringa. Zion and Jerusalem (the one city) answering to "holy cities." <div eID="gen16631" type="x-p"/>
